note: Tatoeba sentences that are correct Icelandic but unsuitable for a course, or whose English translation does not say what the Icelandic says. They are never shown: not in exercises, examples, the dictionary or stories. Checked by scripts/validate-content.mjs.

sentences.10718176: "I love little girls": reads as a sexual remark about children.
sentences.385852: "Since 1990, eleven female students...": the Icelandic says since 1900 (nítjánhundruð).
sentences.511305: "I met him for the first time in three years.": the Icelandic says for the first time, three years ago.
sentences.5003460: "Absence makes the heart grow fonder.": an English proverb for an Icelandic one that says something else (distance makes the mountains blue and the men great).
sentences.1353603: "I expect him to come.": ætlast til (to expect) is a verb of its own; the course would teach it as a form of ætla (to intend).
sentences.382243: "Rice is good with miso soup.": miso is not in Bokmålsordboka, so the sentence can have no checked Bokmål translation. The two sentences made from it (382243-1, 382243-2, content/sentences-made.json) do not need it shown.
sentences.669497: "Hunger is the best spice.": an English proverb for the Icelandic hunger is the best cook; it would teach kokkur as spice.
sentences.881774: "They can fish.": sjóða niður is to can (preserve), but the English reads as being able to fish.
